newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Philippine shares took a breather on Friday, closing in negative territory due to profit-taking in property and blue chip issues which led the gains in recent days, traders said.
"It's a pullback situation from the resilient market we've had the past days," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
"This is a good correction," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
The main index closed 24.24 points lower at 2,881.73. Week-on-week, the index gained 80.12 points from 2,801.61.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 74 to 43. All indices fell.
Of the property issues, index heavyweight Ayala Land Inc closed 50 centavos lower at 23.50 pesos.
Electricity distributor Manila Electric Co (Meralco) B was one of the most actively traded issues and its price fell by four pesos to 131 pesos.
Summit's Liu said he expected the market to open soft next week but said it would likely test a 2,960 resistance level later in the week.
Traders also expected investors to start positioning ahead of the release of first half corporate earnings result.
